note: Register of tabnas runtime dependencies that differ between this repository's ports (tabnas/admin ADR-24). tools/port-deps.cjs fails on a difference that is not listed here, and on an entry that no longer matches the manifests, so the list cannot outlive what it records. Every entry states the ports that have the dependency today, the reason, and the repair.

json.reason: Go and Rust cannot load a plugin by name at run time, so `-p` resolves against a compiled-in registry: go/cli/registry.go imports github.com/tabnas/json/go and registers `tjson.Json` as `json` in `init`, and rs/src/registry.rs registers `tabnas_json::json` as `json` in `builtins`, with tabnas-json in [dependencies] of rs/Cargo.toml; each is its port's only use of the package, and go/cli/run_test.go and rs/tests/cli_test.rs require `-p json a:1` to exit 1. TypeScript: ts/src/jsonic-cli.ts has no import of @tabnas/json and ts/package.json does not declare it; `handle_plugins` loads a `-p` name with `require(name)` and then `require('@tabnas/' + name)`, so `-p json` resolves only where the package is installed, which npm does because it is a required peer of @tabnas/jsonic. Once loaded, `handle_plugins` takes the module's `default` export, which json's ts/src/json.ts sets to `parse` and not to the `json` plugin, so the TypeScript command prints `{"a":1}` for `-p json a:1` and does not enforce strict JSON; DIVERGENCE.md records only the run in which the package was not installed.
json.repair: To agree on having it: ts/package.json would list @tabnas/json as a peer, which adds nothing to an npm install because @tabnas/jsonic already requires it; ts/src would name it only if it also imported the `json` plugin and installed it for `-p json`, as it installs `Debug` for `-d`, which would make `-p json` strict as in Go and Rust. To agree on not having it: go/cli/registry.go and rs/src/registry.rs would stop registering `json` and leave it to `RegisterPlugin` and `register_plugin` in a custom binary, which takes `-p json` out of the stock Go and Rust commands; json would stay in both builds regardless, as a dependency of jsonic. Ruled intentional by the maintainer on 2026-10-06: Go and Rust cannot load a plugin by name at run time, so their stock commands compile json in, while TypeScript requires a `-p` plugin by name; the difference stays and no repair is owed.

parser.reason: Go: go/cli/args.go, registry.go and run.go import github.com/tabnas/parser/go for the registry's `tabnas.Plugin` type and for `tabnas.AsStringMap`, `tabnas.MapToOptions`, `tabnas.Deep`, `tabnas.LexOptions` and `tabnas.Undefined`, and go/go.mod requires it directly. Rust: rs/src/cli.rs, registry.rs, merge.rs, stringify.rs and args.rs use the engine crate's `Plugin`, `PluginError`, `Tabnas`, `Value`, `ListRef` and `MapRef`, with `tabnas` (package tabnas-parser) in [dependencies] of rs/Cargo.toml. TypeScript: ts/src/jsonic-cli.ts has no import of @tabnas/parser, value or type; it takes `Jsonic` and `util` as values and `Plugin` as a type from '@tabnas/jsonic', and ts/package.json keeps the engine as a devDependency so that jsonic's type declarations resolve at build time. The peer was removed on 2026-10-04 (tabnas/jsonic-cli#47), and at run time the engine arrives as a required peer of @tabnas/jsonic.
parser.repair: To agree on having it: ts/package.json would list @tabnas/parser as a peer again, reversing tabnas/jsonic-cli#47, with no import in ts/src to back it. To agree on not having it: go/cli would take the engine's names from the aliases in jsonic's go/engine.go, which has `Plugin`, `MapToOptions`, `Deep`, `LexOptions` and `Undefined` but no `AsStringMap`, and rs/src would need tabnas-jsonic to re-export the engine, where today its rs/src/lib.rs re-exports only `TabnasError` (as `JsonicError`); both wait on a change in tabnas/jsonic. The TypeScript peer was removed under ruling 9 of the handover page in tabnas/parser (doc/handover/README.md); nothing there rules on the Go and Rust ports. Ruled intentional by the maintainer on 2026-10-06: Go and Rust name the engine's types directly, while TypeScript takes them through jsonic; the difference stays and no repair is owed.
